review_basis: registered FDMA combustion source and frozen combustion target contract
semantic distinctness, exam relevance and educational value

decisions.rationale: Detailed combustion definition adds the exothermic-reaction model beyond the existing triangle-element questions.
Chemical-energy to heat/light conversion is a distinct foundational combustion concept.
Heating-driven molecular motion and collision reasoning adds a separate causal path.
Stable-bond formation and energy release is a source-explicit explanation of exothermic combustion.
Lower chemical energy of stable products is a distinct energy-state interpretation from C004's causal explanation.
Ignition source as activation-energy input materially extends the existing generic heat-element question.
Static discharge, impact sparks and lightning broaden practical recognition of ignition sources.
Repeats C006's answer-defining proposition that an ignition source supplies the energy required to initiate combustion; varying the ignition-source examples does not add enough incremental value.
Heat accumulation causing spontaneous ignition is a distinct boundary case with high practical value.
General combustion-chain propagation is the appropriate exam-level representative of the source's chain-reaction subsection.

The exact concentration condition for chain carriers is source-correct but too microscopic relative to the adopted Otsu4 combustion target; C010 preserves the useful chain-reaction concept without this depth.
Heat-induced chain-carrier generation is a microscopic mechanism with insufficient incremental Otsu4 practice value after C006 and C010.
Memorizing H/O/OH as named chain carriers is overly specific for this qualification target despite source correctness.
Chain-carrier termination chemistry exceeds the useful granularity of the Otsu4 combustion target; retain the general chain-reaction concept in C010.
Third-body stabilization by N2/H2O is a specialized kinetic detail and is not justified merely to expand the 600-question target.
Supporter is not limited to atmospheric oxygen; this is a meaningful exception boundary distinct from canonical OTSU4-Q-000005.
Self-reactive substances burning without external supporter provide a separate, source-defined combustion boundary.

collision_review.note: C008 duplicates C006's ignition-energy proposition. C011-C015 are source-correct but rejected as excessive microkinetic detail rather than quota filler. The remaining 11 materially extend canonical 161.

source_review_scope: Final canonical source verification remains separate after integration.
